summary: Free, local-first desktop app where designers edit a real web app visually on a canvas, with Claude Code or Codex making the code changes.

heroCommands.command: Get the desktop app for macOS or Windows from onlook.com/install

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Onlook is an open-source design tool that works on your real codebase. It opens any Git repository on your computer, runs your own dev server, and shows the live app in frames on an infinite canvas. You describe changes in chat, and the Claude Code or ChatGPT/Codex account you connect edits the actual files. You can export artifacts as HTML, PNG, JPEG or PDF.
sixtySeconds.problem: Designs made in mockup tools have to be rebuilt in code. Onlook lets designers shape the real product directly.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for design on your actual app, bring-your-own agent (no Onlook model), local-first operation and one-press pull requests.
requirements: macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) or Windows x64
A Claude Code or ChatGPT/Codex account

overview: Download the desktop app for macOS or Windows. There's no Linux build yet. A source build for Mac is described in SOURCE_BUILD.md and needs no Onlook account or cloud keys.

Point Onlook at a Git repo; it works on a safe worktree copy and runs your dev server. Select frames or double-click elements to guide the agent, view mobile, tablet and desktop side by side, and open pull requests.
The official download collects usage analytics by default (you can turn them off in Settings). It is Apache 2.0 licensed.

firstRun.title: Describe a design
firstRun.body: Type what you want in the chat box.

tutorial.title: Design and export your first draft

steps.title: New Draft
steps.body: Click New Draft in the upper left.

steps.title: Prompt a design
steps.body: Write what you want in the lower-right input and answer the agent's questions.

steps.title: Refine
steps.body: Select frames, or double-click an element for inline chat.

steps.body: Ask the agent to make an Artifact, then export it as HTML/CSS or PNG.
